British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values.
At Holbrook Primary School we take very seriously our responsibility to prepare children for life in modern Britain. We ensure that the fundamental British Values are introduced, discussed and ‘lived out’ through everything we do.
The government defines these values as
The curriculum provides opportunities for further understanding of the British values. In particular, our work with partner schools in other countries provides our pupils with a context in which to explore what it means to be British and to live in Britain. School events are used to promote these values and to provide experiences where the values are demonstrated.
Our belief as staff and governors is that adults should model the attitudes, values and behaviour we wish to see in our children. Our approach to promoting British values is based, firmly, in this belief.

Welcome
Welcome to Holbrook Primary School.
Welcome to our school website which I hope will give you a glimpse of life at Holbrook!
I am immensely proud to be the headteacher here at Holbrook Primary School. Holbrook is a school full of love and care, where every single adult strives for the best for our Holbrook pupils. We are a strong community and have grown even stronger over recent years.
We have around 225 pupils here at Holbrook organised into 8 classes. We have a strong, committed and experienced team of teachers and Learning Support Assistants who all work tirelessly with the aim that every learner is inspired, nurtured and challenged to reach their full potential. We have a strong governing body who support and challenge us, maintaining the strategic direction of the school.
We have been very fortunate to have a new 6-classroom building developed recently and our learning environments make our school a very special place to be.
Choosing your child's Primary School is one of the biggest decisions we make as parents and one that needs to be carefully considered. As such, we would warmly welcome you to Holbrook Primary School where you can have a tour of the school on a 'normal' school day and meet with myself or our Deputy Headteacher to discuss your child and ask any questions you may have. If you would like to have a look around Holbrook to see if it is the right school for your child then please do not hesitate to phone the school office on 01225 753708 to make an appointment.
Headteacher, Holbrook Primary School

Governors
Governance Statement 2024-25
Welcome to our Governors’ section.
Please find below details of how our Governing body is structured, including the names, categories, responsibilities and terms of appointment for each Governor. Our governors can be contacted at governors@holbrook.wilts.sch.uk.
Vicki Cottrell - Headteacher
As the headteacher of Holbrook Primary School I sit on our Full Governing Body. I also sit on our performance and standards committee and our finance and premises committees. I have been a governor here since my appointment in January 2019 and prior to that I was a staff governor at my previous school. I feel very lucky to have an active governing body working alongside me to lead our school forward. They challenge me in our governor's meetings to make sure that we are doing our very best for the children of Holbrook. Outside of school I have a daughter and two very energetic dogs to keep me busy!
Co-Opted Governor. Term of Office ends 31.8.27.
I have been a Governor at Holbrook School since 2013, and the Chair of the Premises sub-committee. I have many years experience working in the education sector. I have seen many changes over the years and realise the importance of long life learning. I have previously served as a Governor at Trowbridge and Wiltshire Colleges, and at the John Bentley School.
During my career I have taught Apprentices, BTEC and A Level students, from electrical, computing maintenance repair to filming techniques courses, and I believe that every young person should be provided with the opportunities to improve their knowledge and skills so that they can achieve their full potential ready for their next step in education and their future prospects. I am involved with GOFISH which expands on this, preparing young people for the challenges of work and becoming young entrepreneurs.
I trained as a professional electrician and progressed to Health & Safety and construction of buildings. My main interest is Trowbridge; documenting it's history/events and I am involved with many local Trowbridge groups.
Rebecca Lockwood Norris
Parent Governor. Term of office ends 30.11.27
I have taken on the role of Parent Governor at Holbrook as I wish to have a positive impact at my children’s school. I am a trained Primary (school) Mentor and, during the time my children have been on role, I have volunteered at Holbrook, listening to children read and being a chaperone on school trips. My professional life has given me good knowledge of governance, compliance, scrutiny and project management, I have also been involved in the administration of grant funding and assisting with community projects; all of which I can apply in my role as a school governor.
Emily Jones - Chair of Governors
Co-Opted Governor. Term of office ends 1.10.27
I have recently been appointed as a Holbrook Governor after my engineering company partnered with GovernorsForSchools, encouraging engagement with schools in our local community. I have a background in civil engineering and project management, and feel I have a variety of skills to bring to the role to help ensure Holbrook continues to be a safe, inspiring and nurturing place to learn. I am passionate about education, its impact on young people, and ensuring they have access to a wide range of opportunities to develop and learn, with a particular passion for STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Maths) subjects. Other than this, I love to be outside and have a very energetic springer spaniel, and a Scout Group, who encourage this as much as possible!
Co-Opted Governor. Term of office ends 17.10.26
Having recently retired after 20 years of providing IT support for Schools, including Holbrook since 2006, I felt I wanted to use my knowledge and skills gained in those 20 years to benefit a local School by becoming a Governor. Holbrook was my first choice as I’ve always found the staff to be friendly but professional and look forward to continuing my relationship with the School as a Governor.
Craig Knight Vice-Chair of Governors
Parent Governor Term of office ends 30.11.27
I have taken on the role of Parent Governor at Holbrook as I wish to help out more at my child's school. I have volunteered at Holbrook on a few occasions and would like to offer more in the future such as jobs around the school which need doing and helping out with the larger contracts that are needed to improve the school grounds and facilities.
Co-Opted Governor. Term of office ends 12.1.29.
I am pleased to be a governor at Holbrook primary school. Before retiring I had many years experience as an HR professional at Wiltshire Council, which included providing HR advice and support to schools and governing bodies.
I live locally and both my daughters went to the school and now my oldest grandchild has just started here.
I'm enjoying reconnecting with the school and supporting by taking on the role of governor.
Staff Governor. Term of office ends 9.3.29
I am a teacher at Holbrook, starting during my placement of my PGCE and obtaining a job shortly after. Holbrook is a special school full of amazing teachers and wonderful children, I want to dedicate more time to Holbrook and support our continued growth during my time as a staff governor. I will be able to share staff news and opinions with governors and share with them the wonderful teaching and learning that takes place at Holbrook. I also lead Science at Holbrook, having completed a Social Science degree. I love forest school and spending time outside.
Co-Opted Governor Term of office ends 7.5.29
I’m very pleased to be joining Holbrook as a Governor. I’m passionate about giving our collective children the best possible launch into life, and am keen to support the Holbrook staff and wider School in that goal. I have good links with other education settings in Trowbridge and wider Wiltshire, and worked with many other Schools in the area supporting their Governors and Academy Councils in delivering good School governance. My professional life takes me all over the world supporting governance, compliance, privacy, and security in businesses, but my heart is in Trowbridge where I live with my wife and 2 sons (who both also attend Holbrook School). In my personal life, I volunteer my time in Schools to pay back my life experiences to the younger generations. I am involved in the Duke of Edinburgh Scheme as an assessor, I also enjoy martial arts and squash to keep fit. My main interest outside business and family life is Lego and have run Lego Club at Holbrook too. Please come and say ‘Hi’ anytime I’m at School - as with all the Holbrook Team I are keen to listen to any and all feedback from School parents, Carers, or the wider School community.
Local Authority Governor - Term of Office ends 14.9.29

Phonics & Reading
At Holbrook we follow the Sounds Write scheme and believe that all children deserve the opportunity to become confident, fluent readers. We begin our phonics lessons from the first day our Reception pupils are in full time. The initial sounds we will be learning are: a, i, m, s, t. These can be used to build words such as it, am, mat, sat, sit. Within our phonics lessons children have the opportunity to learn new sounds, recognise the sounds previously taught, build words using the sounds they have learnt, write words and read stories containing the sounds they already know.

Reading
We follow the Government approved, systematic synthetic phonics programme: Sounds Write for our phonics teaching. Sessions are taught daily as a whole class for 30 minutes from the first full day children attend in Reception through to year 2 and in year 3 until pupils are secure in their phonic knowledge. Children are taught to recognise sounds, the skills of segmenting, blending and phoneme manipulation. As pupils move through the programme they also learn that a spelling can represent more than one sound and that some sounds can be represented in more than one way. Children have opportunity to learn and rehearse these skills daily through a range of lessons within the session. Staff delivering and supporting phonics lessons are all trained in Sounds Write and receive continuous professional development. Children’s progress in phonics is closely tracked and children are regularly assessed. Pupils who require additional support are quickly identified and targeted intervention put in place.
Click here to find out more about Sounds Write
Sounds Write and reading in Early Years
Guided reading in EYFS and year 1 take a different format to the rest of the school with Reception children starting this from the Summer term in preparation for year 1. In year 1, children work in small guided groups with an adult to read and explore a text closely matched to their reading ability and rehearse their phonics skills. Purposeful reading activities are also planned to support reading proficiency. We use a whole class approach to guided reading in Year 2 and KS2. Texts on our reading spine are carefully selected by genre, theme or Author. In all guided reading lessons children read aloud and reading is modelled by an adult. Comprehensions skills such as skimming, scanning and text marking in order to answer questions related to vocabulary, inference, prediction, evaluation, retrieval or summarising known in school as VIPERS. These lessons consist of explicit teaching using model questions and practice questions, guided practice and independent practice. Other written tasks and drama techniques may be used to further their understanding of the text e.g. book reviews, story maps, hot seating etc. One session a week is given over to reading for pleasure, allowing pupils extended time to engage with their text.
Daily story time in all classes is a non-negotiable of the school day. Teachers are supported by the reading leader to ensure they have access to a wide range of books to ignite a love of reading in their class. These books ensure a wide range of genres, cultures and diversity are included in the children’s reading ‘diet’.
Every child at Holbrook has visited the library at least once this year; our children love the library and we have worked hard to form close links with Trowbridge Library.
Our Year 5 & 6 children help the younger children with their reading and to foster a love of reading. We have fortnightly paired reading sessions where the children read to one another and enjoy books together.

Wrap Around Care (before and after school)
Holbrook Primary School run our own high quality Breakfast and After School Clubs.
Click the link to see some of our FREE BREAKFAST CLUB in action! A day in the life of free breakfast club
We are very proud to be an 'early adopter' school for the Government's free breakfast club programme.
Children can attend free breakfast club from 8:15 every day and will have breakfast and an opportunity to play with their friends and connect with their school grown ups before the start of the school day. Our breakfast club foods include cereal, toast, fresh fruit and beans on toast. Our free breakfast club is incredibly popular with over 100 pupils attending every day!
We also offer a 'paid' breakfast club for those who need to drop their children to school a bit earlier in the morning; paid breakfast club starts at 7:30am every day.
At After School Club children have access to a range of activities and the club intends to provide a ‘home from home’ rather than an extension of the school day. We offer a sliding scale for payment to allow parents flexibility and to make childcare as affordable as possible. There are a maximum of 30 places at after school club.
Breakfast Club prices:
7:30am - 8:15am: £3.00 per child
8:15am - 8:25am: Free
After School Club prices:
3:15 – 4:00pm costs £4 per child
3:15 - 5:30pm costs £9.00 per child (this includes a sandwich or a hot meal every day)
Pupils in receipt of Government Pupil Premium funding are offered a subsidised rate for paid breakfast club.
